#2747. Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Week 10: Corey Kiner and Tank Dell step up

Week 9 is almost in the books and the NFL trade deadline is upon us. With rosters about to be shaken up one last time, these are the best players you can get off the waiver wire ahead of Week 10.

The Jets aren't winning games, but Smith is playing exceptional football. He's 13th in EPA per play and fourth in completion percentage over expected. The biggest problem as of late has been a lack of passing volume. Smith hasn't attempted more than 32 passes in a game since Week 3. That should change on Sunday when he takes on the Bills, who are giving up the second-most pass attempts per game this year.

The Steelers are eighth in the NFL in pass attempts per game and Rodgers is 16th in yards per game. He has multiple touchdowns in exactly half of his appearances this year. Now he gets a sneaky shootout spot with the Bengals. Rodgers is one of the better streaming options this week.

It's a truly ugly week of waivers at the quarterback position, so we're going back to the well with Penix. Even after the down week, he sits at a respectable 16th in EPA per play. He gets a Chiefs defense that's been stingy to opposing quarterbacks this year but isn't great efficiency-wise. The Chiefs are allowing the fifth-fewest fantasy points to opposing passers. They only rank 14th in EPA per dropback allowed. Penix is merely a QB2 going forward, but that's all you are going to find off the waiver wire these days.

TreVeyon Henderson's status is unknown as he deals with "unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days." Rhamondre Stevenson is now hurt, having suffered a knee injury in the Pats' blowout loss to the Packers. Both players' statuses for Week 10 are up in the air. Kiner was already forcing a committee between the three when they were healthy. He now has the chance to consolidate work with both players potentially out for an exciting game against the Lions.

Jonathan Taylor could remain a Colt, which would ruin any fantasy potential for McGowan. If he's traded, however, we will get at least an RB2 workload from Indy's backup running back. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 PM ET, so we should have a resolution to this situation before waivers run. McGowan would be a full-send for FAAB purposes if Taylor is traded.

Josh Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the Packers' win over the Patriots. The hope is reportedly that he can play through the issue, but that's not a guarantee. If he can't, Johnson could be the next man up. He was on Sunday with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown. MarShawn Lloyd was notably out for Week 9 and Chris Brooks is practicing but not yet activated from IR. There are a lot of moving parts here, and any one of them could knock Johnson out of the RB3 mix.

Travis Etienne is eligible to return from IR this week, so any Estime streaming potential could be put to bed with a single transaction. If Etienne doesn't return, Estime is in line for another solid workload. He saw 15-of-22 running back carries for the Saints on Sunday, and that was after joining the team for the first time this year on Wednesday. His workload could increase with an additional week of practice.

Cam Skattebo was reportedly pushing to play in Week 9. The Giants ultimately ruled him out before kickoff. Singletary saw 21 carries and three targets. Backup Greg Desrosiers saw three carries and zero targets. Singletary, of course, turned his elite workload into 39 scoreless yards. He's a volume-based RB3 even when he sees every touch, and that might have been a one-week experience.

Johnson's receiving role disappeared in Week 9. He was not targeted once and Kenneth Walker caught four balls for 41 yards and two scores. The good news is that Johnson ran the ball six times for 34 yards and a touchdown. Even more bad news: All six of his attempts came in the fourth quarter. Patrick Mahomes was still on the field, but Walker was just about done for the day once Johnson finally got on the field. He's an intriguing bench stash but nothing more.

The Douglas takeover looks complete after Week 9. The rookie saw 40 percent of Miami's targets and a whopping 61 percent of the air yards. His 34 percent air yards share on the season comfortably leads the team. Douglas is averaging a stellar 2.3 yards per route run. Malik Washington is at a solid 1.6 YPRR while Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr. are both below one. Douglas saw WR1 usage on Sunday and his play suggests that's his role for the taking.

Everyone in Houston ate on Sunday. Dell posted his first 100-yard game since Week 9 of the 2024 season. Kayshon Boutte erupted for 125 yards and two touchdowns. Xavier Hutchinson scored. Nico Collins also got in the end zone, though it happened with a declining role. Dell logged a team-high nine targets. He also led the way in air yards with 133. The downside is that he ran just 55 percent of the available routes. We should expect his role—as measured by routes—to grow as he gets back up to speed, but it could take some time. He is still one of the best waiver wire bets at receiver this week.

It sounds like Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel could both miss another week, meaning Brock Purdy's WR1 is on waivers in almost every fantasy league. Watkins led the 49ers' wideouts with an 87 percent route rate and an 18 percent target share. Demarcus Robinson matched him in targets, but Watkins' 30 percent air yard share easily led the team's receiver room. Both wideouts are in play as deep-cut FLEX options for Week 10.

Jaylen Waddle suffered a concussion on Sunday. Both Bryant and Courtland Sutton—who is rostered in just over half of Yahoo leagues—found the end zone in his absence. Sutton saw nine targets to Bryant's five. The Broncos get their bye in Week 10, meaning Waddle should not miss any time with the concussion. Though Sutton out-targeted Bryant in Week 9, that could flip coming out of the break. Bryant is averaging 1.6 yards per route run this year compared to 1.0 for Sutton. Bryant's the second-best receiver on the team and is gaining steam headed into the team's week off. Sean Payton might finally treat him like the WR2 in Week 11.

Jefferson has to be mentioned after leading the Commanders in every receiving category via a 5-58-1 receiving line. His seven targets and 88 air yards also led the team. He might be the team's WR1 with Terry McLaurin out. He might also turn back into a pumpkin next week. I would bet on the latter with my FAAB dollars and waiver priorities, but if you're truly desperate for a WR5, he's on the menu.

Waller erupted for 90 yards and a touchdown on eight grabs in Week 9. It was his first game with more than one catch since Week 4. He did, however, hit a season-high route rate of 67 percent. His previous season-high came in Week 8 at 66 percent. Waller's role, while not great, does appear to be on the rise. He's functionally the team's WR3, but fantasy managers get to play him at tight end.

McLaurin went down with a season-ending injury a few snaps into Week 6. From that game onward, Okonkwo has an 83 percent route rate with 22 percent of the Commanders' targets. He has also seen a quarter of the team's end zone looks. It's not flashy, but he's looking like a high-end TE2.

Barner found the end zone twice on Sunday, once via a tush push and a second time through the air. He'll be a popular name on waivers this week, but his role remained middling at best. He earned a 15 percent target share—one point above his season-long rate—and only ran 66 percent of the routes, which was actually a season-low mark for him. Barner is still nothing more than a touchdown-or-bust TE2.

#2746. Tennessee loses sack-leader Tyree Weathersby to season-ending injury

The Tennessee Volunteers are playing some great football and have found themselves right in the middle of the College Football Playoff hunt here in mid-November, but unfortunately, they will have to go the rest of the way without one of their best defensive linemen on the field.

According to a report from On3's Austin Price, defensive lineman Tyree Weathersby is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season after suffering a knee injury in Saturday's win over the Kentucky Wildcats. Weathersby leads Tennessee in sacks this year with seven, and has 20 tackles and 8.5 tackles for loss to go along with it.

Going forward, there is still a ton of talent on Tennessee's defensive line, but they are going to need to step up in a big way as this team looks to make a final push toward the postseason.

The Vols got a huge win over Kentucky on Saturday, but they face Texas A&M, LSU, and Vanderbilt over the final three weeks of the season, and likely need to win out in order to lock up a playoff spot.

#2745. Another Lions Defensive Back Target Comes Off the Board

The Detroit Lions secondary came into deadline week as this roster's clearest need, and one of the safeties most often floated as a fit for Detroit is now off the board. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday that the Atlanta Falcons are trading former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The trade deadline is 4 p.m. ET Tuesday.

That is a hefty price for a rental. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Atlanta is covering most of what is left of Bates' salary, and Bates is in the final year of his contract, so he becomes a free agent at the end of the season. Jacksonville is 6-2 and bulking up on the defensive side of the football for a playoff run. Atlanta, at 3-6, sold.

Atlanta Falcons free safety Jessie Bates (3) pursues Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'marr Chase (1) in the fourth quarter of the NFL International Week 9 game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Cincinnati Bengals at Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. The Bengals won the international matchup, 34-17. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Bates was never reported as a Detroit pursuit. ESPN's Dan Graziano wrote ahead of the deadline that he did not believe Atlanta was trying to trade him at all, and ESPN's deadline preview lists secondary help as the Lions' deadline goal without naming him. The fit was the appeal, and DSN floated him as a target on Oct. 2.

The defensive back Detroit did chase went somewhere else too. After the Pittsburgh Steelers sent cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys, head coach Dan Campbell said on Oct. 2, per Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News, "Brad, he's been on it for a while. That's been ongoing. Everything's got to align right. Cowboys did what they wanted to do. We were very much in on it." Five weeks later, Holmes still has not made a move.

Three NFC teams in Detroit's way have. The Chicago Bears sent 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth to Tennessee for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The Seattle Seahawks gave Indianapolis a 2027 third and a 2028 fifth for guard Quenton Nelson. The San Francisco 49ers got defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Colts for a 2027 fourth.

The Lions are 6-2 after grinding out a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, and the defense has been better over the last three weeks. With that being said, Detroit can not stand pat at the trade deadline and expect things will be just fine for them.

Through nine games Bates has 60 total tackles, three forced fumbles, one interception, four passes defensed and a fumble return for a touchdown. Detroit could have had a safety duo of Bates and Brian Branch, who is off the injury report. Kerby Joseph is still on the physically unable to perform list with a knee injury and was ruled out against Miami, and safety Thomas Harper is on injured reserve, which leaves defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard thin behind Branch.

Jacksonville now has a safety who has forced three fumbles in nine games. Detroit has one more day to find help.

#2740. 2026-27 NHL season predictions: Expert picks for Stanley Cup playoffs, champion and major awards this season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2739. Saints vs. Browns: Winners and Losers from New Orleans’ thrilling win

The New Orleans Saints found their third win of the season on Sunday, beating the Cleveland Browns en route to taking the lead in the NFC South.

The win wasn't pretty, and there's plenty to work on, but there is light at the end of the tunnel after New Orleans' victory out of the bye.

Just two weeks ago, the Saints running backs ran for 11 rushing yards on 14 attempts. Going into the bye, that was the only conversation surrounding the Saints. They couldn't run the ball all season, and it was on full display in another country.

Coming out of the bye, the Saints lucked out and found a way to bring running back Audric Estime back on waivers. In his first game back with New Orleans, Estime ran for 72 yards on 15 carries, averaging 4.8 yards per carry and scoring a touchdown.

While Travis Etienne's return is on the horizon, Estime has likely found a role with the Saints where he'll handle the bulk of the carries until he comes back.

Phew. The Saints have a dangerous pass rush combo. We all knew about Chase Young, who has 8 sacks in 8 games this season. But Carl Granderson has feasted off the attention Young brings and has brought his season sack total to 7.5 sacks.

In the win against the Browns, Granderson logged 2 sacks and 2 tackles for loss. He was a game changer for the Saints on Sunday, and entered the week with a chip on his shoulder after a viral video of Shedeur Sanders seemingly laughing when asked a question about the Saints' defense.

While Sanders says he wasn't laughing at the Saints' defense, it opened the opportunity to add more motivation for the defense, and Granderson himself took it personally. If the former undrafted free agent can continue to play like this, New Orleans will end the season with two of the top three sack leaders.

Sunday's matchup against the Browns was favored for the Saints secondary, who were facing a second-year quarterback in Sanders. The 2025 fifth-round pick got his first start of the 2026 season and faced the fierce Saints pass rush.

The Saints pass rush did their job, but the secondary was outplayed in the biggest moments. From Denzel Boston missing Kool-Aid McKinstry to Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. failing to tackle KC Concepcion after allowing a big catch that turned into a touchdown, we didn't see the plays we needed from the secondary against Tetairoa McMillan.

What stands out the most for me, however, is the Saints' inability to force takeaways. This was a prime opportunity to force takeaways and come away with a dominant win. New Orleans, however, lost the turnover battle, losing two fumbles and not forcing any turnovers themselves.

From Jordyn Tyson's first reception turning into a fumble three yards from the end zone, to Barion Brown running backwards before losing the ball himself, the Saints are beating themselves. The Saints are -6 on the season in the turnover battle, and it continues to get further away from them.

#2734. MLB rumors: Mets' Bo Bichette makes contract decision, familiar All-Star back on trade block

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is only two days old and already the hot stove moves and rumors are coming in. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and here are the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

As expected, Mets infielder Bo Bichette has picked up his $42 million player option for 2027, reports The Athletic. He holds another $42 million player option for 2028. Still only 28, Bichette had a poor first season in Queens, posting a .702 OPS with 18 home runs while showing growing pains as he transitioned from shortstop over to third base.

For now, the Mets are set on the infield with Bichette at third, Francisco Lindor at short, and Marcus Semien at second. They must figure out first base, and it is possible they will make a trade to shake up that veteran infield. Moving Semien would be ideal, but it may not be doable. Lindor's name figures to pop up in trade rumors against this offseason.

The Diamondbacks are expected to listen to offers for second baseman Ketel Marte, reports the Arizona Republic. The D-backs entertained trade offers last offseason, but were unable to find a match. Marte has full no-trade protection and can direct where he lands, if he wants to leave Arizona at all. His desire to change teams is unknown.

Marte, 33, had a down year by his standards in 2026. He also went AWOL in August, prompting the D-backs to put him on the restricted list. Manager Torey Lovullo later revealed it was the fourth straight season Marte missed a game without permission. Beyond the on-field fit, teams will have to weigh the potential clubhouse impact and headaches.

The Seibu Lions in Japan will make right-hander Kaima Taira available to MLB teams via the posting system this offseason, the team announced Friday. The posting is expected to be made official in the coming days. Once that happens, Taira will have 45 days to negotiate and sign with an MLB team, otherwise he will return to Japan in 2027.

We ranked Taira as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason. Here's our write-up:

Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man.

Taira, 27 next month, threw 146 innings with a 1.36 ERA and 141 strikeouts this past season. He actually had higher ERAs as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, though he has been excellent throughout his career in Japan, and has the bat-missing power stuff that tends to translate well to MLB. Taira figures to be highly sought after in the coming weeks.

The trading season resumed Thursday and the Red Sox were involved in the offseason's first two trades. First, they sent utility man Nate Eaton to the Athletics for minor-league righty Jareth Rayo, the team announced. The A's recently named former Red Sox assistant general manager Taylor Smith their new president of baseball operations. His first move was bringing in Eaton, a player he's presumably familiar with given their overlapping time in Boston.

Next, the Red Sox traded infielder Tsung-Che Cheng to the Tigers for cash, the team announced. Cheng, 25, is a glove-first utility man who appeared in 14 games with Boston this past season. Both the Cheng and Eaton trades open up 40-man roster spots for the Red Sox, who still must open three more spots to accommodate their seven players on the 60-day injured list. They must be activated no later than this coming Monday.

#2733. Steelers 2026 mid-season awards: Who is Pittsburgh’s MVP?

We have reached the mid-season point of the 2026 NFL regular season (it always goes by too fast). The Pittsburgh Steelers have been one of the top teams in the league through nine weeks, sitting at the top of the AFC North with a 6-2 record while holding the No. 4 seed in the AFC playoff picture.

Over the course of this week, our staff here at Behind the Steel Curtain will roll out our mid-season awards, which begins today with the Steelers' 2026 mid-season MVP.

Joey Bray – RB Jaylen Warren: This award simply cannot go to anyone else. Warren was third in the NFL in scrimmage yards through eight weeks of play, and remains in fifth after the bye week. Plus, he is doing so with incredible efficiency. On an offense that lacks weapons on the outside, Warren is the engine that has the Steelers' offense on an upward trend heading into the second half of their season.

Austin Bechtold – RB Jaylen Warren: Warren entered the bye week with more rushing yards than Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor. His 6.93 yards per touch this season is the highest in football and 1.31 yards higher than the next closest running back (Bijan Robinson). Warren is the best weapon in the Steelers arsenal and has been revolutionary for an offense that has been relatively stagnant for half a decade. I'd be happy with Warren receiving additional carries, as long as his body can hold up. Warren seems like the obvious answer, but I think T.J Watt and Jalen Ramsey also have case.

Ryan Parish – C Zach Frazier: It was tempting to put Jaylen Warren here, but Frazier is so crucial to what Warren and the rest of the offense do, he has to get the nod. He's also the Steeler with the best case at being the best at his position in the entire NFL.

Ryland Bickley – C Zach Frazier: I'm torn between Frazier and Jaylen Warren here, but will go with the star center as he's been arguably the best at his position in the entire league this year. And hey, when it's a toss-up like this, why not give the offensive line some much-needed credit? Frazier has anchored the group that's been the story of the team's season thus far.

Mike Nicastro – RB Jaylen Warren: This one could certainly be up for debate, but my vote goes to Jaylen Warren. Warren has been the igniter of Pittsburgh's offense and arguably the biggest reason the Steelers are sitting at 6-2. Whether it's creating explosive plays, keeping the offense ahead of the chains or providing a spark when the passing game struggles, Warren has consistently delivered. Through eight games, Warren has rushed for 704 yards on 119 carries, averaging an impressive 5.9 yards per attempt. He's also added 294 receiving yards on 25 receptions, giving him 998 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Warren has become the engine of this offense. While there are other deserving candidates, it's difficult to overlook the impact he's had on a team that has won four consecutive games.

Jarrett Bailey – RB Jaylen Warren: It looks like I'm the tie-breaker here, but I'm going with Warren. Even after the bye week, he's fifth in the NFL in scrimmage yards and has emerged as one of the game's three-five best running backs. Without his productivity, there is zero chance the Steelers are 6-2.

#2732. UConn men's basketball coach Dan Hurley's Wagner roots still resonate

STORRS — Long before the sold-out crowds, national championships and viral sideline outbursts, Dan Hurley was building the foundation of his coaching legacy at a tiny gym on Staten Island.

The players who survived it still laugh about it today.

"We were crash dummies," former Wagner guard Tyler Murray said. "We were literally test dummies to see how hard he could push, how close to the line he could teeter with, whether that was compliance or our mental capacity."

Exclusive interview with Jordan Page: Why five-star Jordan Page committed to UConn men's basketball | Exclusive

Silas Demary Jr's heroics: UConn men's basketball gets revenge as Silas Demary Jr. powers win over Michigan

Hurley's time at Wagner was the proving ground for his relentless standards, constant competition, and emotional intensity that have since carried him to the top of college basketball. What began as an experiment at one of Division I's struggling programs became the blueprint for a coach who would eventually transform UConn into a national powerhouse.

Ahead of UConn's matchup with Wagner on Monday night, former Seahawk players Tyler Murray and Latif Rivers spoke to the Bulletin and reflected on Hurley's two seasons coaching the Seahawks.

They described a coach whose methods could be exhausting, blunt and, at times, overwhelming. But 15 years removed from playing for Hurley, both said Hurley's impact has gone beyond basketball.

"He was a guy who could truly get on you and tell you about yourself and say it in the most vulgar way," Rivers said. "But he always lets you know that he cared and that there was a method to his madness. So, it's a lot of lessons that I learned playing for him that I apply in my everyday life."

Hurley arrived at Wagner after nine years as the head coach at high school powerhouse St. Benedict's Prep in Newark, New Jersey. He built a reputation of success early, amassing a record of 223–21, coaching four McDonald's All-Americans and establishing the program as one of the best in the country.

Hurley accepted the job to coach Wagner in 2010, taking over a team that won just five games the year before. Hurley had built a reputation as a great developer of young talent, but reviving a program from irrelevancy was another challenge unto itself.

"I actually knew Danny since I was kid," Rivers said. "Being from Jersey, you knew who the Hurleys were and the things Danny was able to do at St. Benedict's. But to be honest, I never even knew what a Wagner was. It was this small school in Staten Island, but the thing I did know was that Danny was coaching the team."

From the moment he arrived, Hurley attacked the rebuild with the same intensity that would later become synonymous with UConn's success.

In his first season, he led Wagner to a 13-win improvement. A year later, Wagner won 25 regular season games and finished second in the Northeast Conference standings, completing one of the most successful turnarounds in the country.

"It was a group that took a five-win program, maybe literally the worst Division One team in the country and two years later had 25 regular season wins," Hurley said at practice on Sunday. "That was one of my favorite years I've ever had in coaching."

The transformation was fueled by a culture that rarely allowed players to let up.

"We were battling. Everything was a competition," Murray said. "Every chance to win a drill was counted. We counted every single thing, and that just bred its own competition within us. I think it grew us all and our bonded us just to see how far he's gone with it, but also some of the rituals that he keeps doing wherever he goes."

The culture built at Wagner was the early version of the formula Hurley would establish to build championship teams. Murray and Rivers quickly learned that every possession, every drill and every detail mattered.

Hurley was not building the program alone.

His brother and legendary Duke point guard, Bobby Hurley, served on the Wagner staff before eventually beginning his own head coaching career. Together, the brothers brought instant credibility to a program that had little national recognition at the time.

But while both bring intense personalities to coaching, Rivers said their dynamic was exactly what the Seahawks needed.

"They were yin and yang," Rivers said. "Danny was the crazier one, and then Bobby was the one who was the voice of reason."

The demands could be overwhelming, and Hurley's abrasive style ratcheted up everything Wagner did. But years later, Murray said the message behind every delivery is what has stayed with him the most.

"If you really read through how it was being delivered, it was from a place of love and for the betterment of the team and some personal growth as a man," Murray said. "There's not really beating around the bush. There's not a lot of moments where he's trying to put it in a pleasant way. It's coming out. But it's generally from a great place that's trying to help or encourage."

For the players who helped lay the foundation at Wagner, the championships, Final Fours and the national acclaim that have followed Hurley have been less surprising than they have been validating.

When Hurley finishes his career, he will be widely regarded as one of the sport's best. His resume is already good enough to warrant a trip to the hall of fame and he is only 53.

When asked if he could have ever expected Hurley was going to be this good, Rivers said there was no doubt.

"I knew that anywhere that he went as a coach, he was gonna put his imprint on it," Rivers said. "He's a winner. I wouldn't have been surprised at all if you came up to me and told me that he would one day be one of the greats."

This article originally appeared on The Bulletin: UConn men's basketball coach Dan Hurley's Wagner roots still resonate

#2730. Astros hire Randy Flores as new general manager as offseason filled with questions begins in Houston

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Houston Astros' search for a new head of baseball operations has ended with the hiring of Randy Flores as general manager. The 51-year-old Flores had been an assistant general manager with the St. Louis Cardinals. In Houston, Flores replaces Dana Brown, who was let go in late August. Flores becomes the fourth head of baseball operations to serve under Astros owner Jim Crane.

"Randy has had a huge impact on the Cardinals over the last 10 seasons," Crane said in a statement released by the club. "Throughout the entire interview process, we've been thoroughly impressed with Randy and his background in scouting and player acquisition. We're happy to welcome Randy and his family to the Astros and we can't wait to get to work on bringing another championship to Houston."

Added Flores: "I am excited and grateful for this amazing opportunity. The Astros have a long winning tradition under Jim Crane, and I look forward to contributing to the success.  I want to thank the Cardinals organization for the opportunities and support that made this next chapter possible. My family and I are excited to make Houston home."

Flores for roughly a decade served as scouting director for the Cardinals and was tasked with running their draft. He added the assistant GM title in 2018 and saw his portfolio of responsibilities expand within the last year.

Flores takes over an Astros organization beset by uncertainty. With an aging roster and after several key departures over the years, the Astros have seen their season-long win total decline for four straight years. This past season, the Astros eked out the American League Central title but finished with a .500 record and a negative run differential. In terms of success and roster strength, they're a long way from their dynasty years of 2017-22. It's not certain whether the Astros moving forward will try to squeeze out another season of relevance or embrace a rebuild, but either path will have its challenges.

Speaking of challenges, Crane and his trusted advisor Jeff Bagwell have been an increasingly meddlesome presence in recent years, and it's unclear to what degree Flores will have autonomy in his role. Whatever the future holds, Flores' first major decision is filling the managerial vacancy. After the end of the regular season, Crane opted not to renew the contract of former manager Joe Espada.

Prior to beginning his front office career, Flores spent parts of eight seasons in the majors as a left-handed reliever. In 2006, he earned a World Series ring as a member of that Cardinals team.

#2728. MLB rumors: Padres decline option on key rotation piece, Korean star to be posted

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is only four days old and already the hot stove moves and rumors are coming in. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and here are the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Sunday's hot stove happenings.

San Diego's top two starters are now free agents. Two days after Michael King exercised an opt-out clause to become a free agent, the Padres declined their $14 million club option on Nick Pivetta, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Had the Padres picked up the option, Pivetta would have held an $18 million player option for 2028. That surely factored into the team's decision.

Pivetta, 34 in February, missed roughly five months with a flexor strain this past season. He returned late in the season and pitched reasonably well in six starts spanning September and the postseason. The San Diego Union-Tribune notes the Padres still have concerns about Pivetta's elbow, but could re-sign him to a new contract with a lower salary and/or no player option.

San Diego signed Pivetta to what amounted to a two-year, $23 million contact with two players options in February 2025. The flexor strain triggered an injury clause that converted the 2027 player option into a club option. We ranked Pivetta as the offseason's 43rd-best free agent.

As expected, the Orioles have declined their $20 million club option for center fielder Luis Robert Jr., reports ESPN. They will pay him a $2 million buyout, so it was functionally an $18 million decision. Robert suffered a hamstring injury and played only three games with the O's after being claimed off waivers from the Mets in late September.

Now 29, Robert again had multiple stints on the injured list this past season. He continued to punish lefties and play solid center field defense when healthy, but injuries have limited him to only 271 of 489 possible regular-season games from 2024-26. We did not rank Robert among our top 50 free agents, though he is an interesting upside play given his age.

The Hanwha Eagles of the Korea Baseball Organization will post star third baseman Si-Hwan Roh for MLB teams this offseason, reports Yonhap News Agency. Roh signed the richest deal in KBO history in February (11 years and $23 million), though as part of the deal, the Eagles agreed to post him this offseason, and Roh agreed to return to the team once his MLB stint is over.

Roh, 26, has been one of the KBO's best players the last several years. He hit .283/.360/.505 with 29 home runs in 2026, and has averaged 35 home runs per 162 games since 2023. Roh is considered a reliable but unspectacular defender at third, plus he has first base experience as well. This free agent class is very thin at the hot corner. Roh should generate a good deal of interest.

KBO players get a 30-day negotiating window once officially posted. If Roh does not sign with an MLB team during the 30-day window, he will return to the Eagles. It's possible that Roh, a right-handed hitter, will eclipse his $23 million guarantee with the Eagles over just a handful of years with an MLB team.

The Astros have acquired Triple-A righty reliever Evan Reifert from the Rays for cash, reports the Tampa Bay Times. Houston is likely to add him to their 40-man roster to protect him from the Rule 5 Draft. The Rays did not have the roster space to do that, so they traded for cash rather than lose him for nothing. Reifert, 27, has an excellent slider and used it to strike out 81 batters in 58 Triple-A innings in 2026. He should spend time in Houston's bullpen next season.

#2727. Fantasy Football Stock Report: Jordan Love on a heater while Lions' depth receivers struggle coming out of Week 9

As I write this on Sunday night, 14 of 15 Week 9 games are in the books (with Monday night remaining) and the fantasy football season is now past the halfway point. Still, things are changing every week. Promising improvements. Concerning trends. Performances that change our early outlook on players and teams. As always, some of these shifting perspectives will have permanent ramifications in fantasy football.

With that in mind, I've compiled another full fantasy stock report. These are the most notable risers and fallers heading into Week 10.

I confess, I did not love C.J. Stroud for this Sunday, given how tough the Chargers had been against quarterbacks. My bad.

Stroud had one of his best games as a pro, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns (with one INT), plus 20 rushing yards just for kicks. His 36.36 fantasy points were the second-most of his career ... and it wasn't an aberration. Stroud now has 20+ fantasy points in four of his last five games and is averaging 24.18 PPG over that span. A big part of the story: Tank Dell's breakout after a multi-year absence and a monster game from Kayshon Boutte. Nico Collins also had 55 yards and a TD, but it was Boutte's 4-125-2 and Dell's 4-105-1 that really made the difference (oh, and Xavier Hutchinson snagged a TD as well).

This is an eclectic, but clearly talented, receiving corps and Stroud is making it work to his advantage (and that of his fantasy managers). Dell is a great waiver wire add — and/or Boutte in deeper leagues — and Stroud might be a strong trade target before your league's deadline, considering he might be another manager's QB2.

Speaking of monster quarterback performances, Jordan Love might be the hottest QB in the league right now. He looked unstoppable on Sunday against the Patriots, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns, for a 153.2 passer rating and 36.18 fantasy points. He's now topped 21 points in four of his last five games — with 17.96 in the fifth — and is averaging 24.04 points per game over that span.

The connections with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are both exquisite right now, as arguably the only trio playing better is Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins for the Bengals ... and it's close. Over the entire season, Love has thrown for fewer than 270 yards just twice, both in the first month. His 2,618 passing yards lead the league and have him on pace for — double-checks math — 4,945 yards on the year. Now, of course, the ultimate test comes next week against the Vikings — I would frankly consider sitting him despite the red-hot stretch against this Minnesota defense — and then Love has his bye in Week 11. But with a playoff stretch that includes the Bills, Dolphins, Bears and Texans, Love could be pretty well positioned to win fantasy managers a title in 2026.

Jonah Coleman was the hottest name in fantasy the past week — I called him the waiver-wire pickup of the year on air — and he did not disappoint in Week 9. Despite surprising inefficiency on the ground — considering the matchup with Carolina — Coleman totaled 88 scrimmage yards (with four catches) and a nine-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. He played a whopping 81.5% of the snaps and handled 81% of the running back carries, putting to bed any lingering concerns about J.K. Dobbins "vulturizing" the rookie (yes, I just made that word up). That's not just "head-of-the-committee" volume, that's true bell-cow volume. Yes, it's possible that when RJ Harvey eventually returns from IR, Coleman might lose a bit of his receiving upside, but that's weeks away. It's also possible the Broncos trade for a running back (Jonathan Taylor?) ... and that might be hours away, depending on when you read this. But hopefully that doesn't happen.

As long as Coleman makes it through Tuesday afternoon as the RB1, he's going to be a league-winner down the stretch. Congratulations if you picked him, kudos if you drafted him and if you're in neither of those positions and can trade for him on Tuesday at 4:01 p.m. ET, do it.

Frankly, Breece Hall just needed to make it back to the field for his Stock to be Up after a five-week absence. But he did more than that, out-carrying Braelon Allen 15-to-8, matching Allen's 4.1 yards per carry and slightly outperforming him as a receiver (with three catches for 26 yards). Given how well Allen had played in Hall's stead, there was some realistic concern that he would be relegated to a pass-catching role or to a distant No. 2 slot in a frustrating committee.

Hall did trail Allen in snap share (43.5% to 58.1%), but that's likely a side effect of the Jets easing Hall back into action. As long as neither back is moved at the trade deadline — which should reportedly be the case — I'd expect Hall to retake the lead in snap share and for his fantasy production to reflect that moving forward. Allen has played well enough that Hall's once-upon-a-time bell-cow workload is probably a thing of the past, but 19 opportunities in his first game back — in a game the Jets lost 35-12, by the way — is extremely encouraging. He should be a strong RB2 moving forward.

In this week's version of the ongoing "Which 49ers Wide Receiver Do We Like?" mini-game, it was Jordan Watkins who stepped up big to the tune of four catches for 86 yards and a touchdown. He's now topped 50 receiving yards in three of the four games he's played this season and is averaging 22.4 yards per reception this season. Dig a little deeper and you get this nugget: Watkins leads all players with 100+ routes run in yards per target at 17.2.

And while he hadn't been consistently involved enough for that to matter much earlier in the year, he led San Francisco with 26 routes on Sunday and tied George Kittle for the team high in catches. Obviously, Mike Evans will return soon and Watkins will drop to the WR2 spot at best, with Kittle and Christian McCaffrey also heavily involved. However, as we've seen with Brock Purdy at the helm, there is room for fantasy goodness a ways down this depth chart. Watkins should be heavily added off waivers, and if Evans struggles to return or stay healthy, he might have weekly starter upside down the stretch.

Kyren Williams had stayed strong for fantasy amid the rise of Blake Corum by finding the end zone more often than not. Without that TD in Week 9, the Rams RB1A — theoretically — scored just 7.6 points on 61 scrimmage yards. It's his second game with single-digit fantasy points over the last month, and Williams has averaged just 11.3 PPG over that stretch after scoring 19.2 PPG over the first five weeks. And while he did play more snaps and out-carried Corum 15-to-11 on Sunday, the latter back was far more efficient, logging 5.3 yards per carry and scoring the goal-line touchdown, while Williams clocked in at just 3.0 yards per carry.

Williams is still a borderline must-start — you'd have to be stocked at running back to sit him in any given week — but the ceiling has been clearly and noticeably lowered with Corum's ongoing involvement (especially in the red zone). If you can get low-end RB1 (or even high-end RB2) value for Williams in a trade, it might not be a terrible idea.

I very actively and vocally disliked Ollie Gordon II in this matchup with the Lions' pass-funnel defense, so the 6.9 fantasy points on an inefficient 17 touches doesn't surprise me. That said, it was his second consecutive game with exactly 6.9 points and has clearly revealed the weakness in Gordon's game: he has no receiving upside (23 total receiving yards on the year) and is not dominant enough to beat strong run defenses. That means that, from week-to-week, Gordon's ceiling is going to depend heavily on touchdowns and opposing defenses.

The good news there is that his remaining schedule is relatively soft, so it's possible we see more "good Gordon" than "meh Gordon" down the stretch. The bad news is that there is a clear cap on his fantasy upside: even in his great outings, Gordon still hasn't scored more than 17 fantasy points in a game this season. He's a low-end RB2 with a high(ish) volume-based floor, but he's still a relatively average back in the Miami Dolphins offense.

While Amon-Ra St. Brown was excellent and Jahmyr Gibbs was good enough on Sunday, Sam LaPorta had another fantasy dud and Jameson Williams came crashing back to earth. LaPorta now has fewer than six fantasy points in three straight games and is averaging just 4.2 points per game since the Week 6 bye. It's been a strange change of fortunes after he scored 14+ in three of four weeks heading into the bye, and it was particularly discouraging in what has been a great tight-end matchup with Miami.

As for Williams, he finally did the Jameson Williams thing — after four straight excellent games, with 13+ fantasy points in each, he logged a 4.5-point dud with just one catch (and one rush) all day. The matchup was much worse for Williams than for LaPorta, so we'll give him a little grace there, but this was a stark and long-awaited reminder that Williams is prone to disappear every now and then.

By all accounts, Goff and Co. should bounce back in future weeks, though they do have the Patriots on deck, the Buccaneers in the hole and another meeting with the Vikings in Week 15. Just keep in mind: this offense runs through Gibbs and St. Brown, and everyone else will have down days.

In his first five games with Michael Penix Jr. this year, Drake London averaged 6.4 receptions and 107.2 receiving yards per game ... and scored his lone touchdown of the year. Over the last two weeks, London has six catches and 76 receiving yards combined. He had seen 10+ targets in four of those first five games and has now seen just 11 total targets these last two games. This was his fourth straight game with fewer than 70 receiving yards, and while that's a relatively high bar, his lack of touchdowns requires massive yardage to compensate for fantasy. For reference, every other player with at least 480 receiving yards has multiple touchdown receptions this season — London has 692 yards (eighth in the league) and just one score.

To make matters worse, London's next three weeks are just about as bad as you can get: the Chiefs, the bye, the Vikings. Even if he does return to WR1 upside in December or so, London is entering an extremely ugly stretch. If you can, try to trade him for a more consistent WR1 — maybe Tee Higgins — before a couple more duds or your league's trade deadline make him unmovable.

#2724. Mets legend Jerry Koosman dies at 83: Pitcher helped New York win 1969 World Series

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Mets team Hall of Famer and two-time All-Star Jerry Koosman died Sunday morning in Osceola, Wisconsin, the team announced. He was 83. The Mets say Koosman battled multiple illnesses before his death.

"Kooz was one of the greatest pitchers in team history and a beloved member of the Mets family," Mets owners Alex and Steve Cohen said in a statement. "The 1969 Miracle Mets were filled with heroes, and the special southpaw from Appleton, Minnesota, was central to their success. He was a fierce competitor on the field, and respected teammate in the clubhouse. His legendary performance in the World Series helped the Mets secure their first Championship in team history. On behalf of the entire Mets organization, we extend our heartfelt condolences to Jerry's family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him."

The Mets discovered Koosman while he was pitching for the United States Army and signed him to a contract in August 1964. He made his MLB debut in April 1967 and moved into the rotation full-time the next season. Koosman threw 263 ⅔ innings with a 2.08 ERA as a rookie in 1968, which earned him an All-Star Game selection and MVP votes, and a second-place finish in the Rookie of the Year voting behind Hall of Famer Johnny Bench.

In 1969, Koosman was again an All-Star, throwing 241 innings with a 2.28 ERA. He was New York's No. 2 starter in the postseason between Hall of Famers Tom Seaver and Nolan Ryan. Koosman made two starts for the Miracle Mets in the World Series, including the Game 5 clincher against the Baltimore Orioles. He allowed three runs in the complete game win and recorded all but one possible out in his two World Series starts.

From 1968-76, Koosman was simply one of the best pitchers in the game, pitching to a 2.94 ERA and averaging 223 innings per season. The Mets traded him to the Minnesota Twins for Jesse Orosco in December 1978 and Koosman finished his career with stints for the Twins (1979-81), Chicago White Sox (1981-83), and Philadelphia Phillies (1984-85).

Koosman retired following the 1985 season with a 222-209 record and a 3.36 ERA that is 39th among AL/NL pitchers with at least 3,500 career innings. He ranks 35th all-time in strikeouts (2,556), 40th all-time in starts (527), 48th all-time in innings (3,839 ⅓), and 77th all-time in pitching WAR (57.0). Koosman went to two All-Star Games and finished second to Randy Jones in the 1976 Cy Young voting.

The Mets inducted Koosman into their Hall of Fame in 1989 and retired his No. 36 in 2021. His 140 wins are the most in franchise history among left-handers and third in team history overall, behind Seaver (198) and Dwight Gooden (157). Koosman is second in Mets history in innings (behind Seaver) and third in strikeouts (behind Seaver and Gooden).

Koosman fell off the Baseball Writers Association of America's Hall of Fame ballot in 1991, his first year of eligibility.

#2723. NFL Monday Night Football preview: Vikings defense gets a tough test vs. Josh Allen and Bills

Josh Allen has been the best quarterback in the NFL so far this season, at least by some key metrics. But he hasn't faced a defense like the Minnesota Vikings.

And the Vikings have been the best defense in the NFL. Yet, they haven't faced a quarterback like Allen.

The Vikings host the Buffalo Bills on Monday night in a fun matchup of 6-1 teams. Allen's ability to beat the Vikings' many blitzes will be the key to the game. Nobody else has been to do it. The Chicago Bears are on a roll offensively, but the Bears scored just three points at home against the Vikings' aggressive defense back in Week 2. Minnesota has allowed the lowest EPA (expected points added) per play among all NFL defenses this season. Allen has the highest EPA per play among all quarterbacks.

While the headlining matchup will be Allen against the Vikings' defense led by their coordinator Brian Flores, there will be intrigue when the Vikings have the ball too. The Vikings' offense, led by Carson Wentz as normal starting quarterback Kyler Murray sits out with a sore hamstring, will have to find a way to move the ball. Minnesota is 6-1 despite being 27th in points per game and 29th in yards per game. Murray has been a big disappointment, and perhaps the Vikings didn't want to rush him back from the hamstring injury to see if Wentz can give the offense a spark. It's possible against a suspect Bills defense that has allowed the third-most passing yards per game this season.

But everyone will be tuning in to see what Allen, the former MVP, does against Minnesota's defense. With a big game, Allen will remain at the front of the pack to win another MVP award. And Buffalo will look like an even stronger Super Bowl contender.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is having another MVP-worthy season. (AP Photo/Sue Ogrocki)

The 2026 NFC North looks like a division that could send all four teams to the playoffs. It's deep from top to bottom. Even though the Vikings are 6-1 they can't feel safe with the Bears, Packers and Lions all playing well. The Bills also will be pushed in the AFC East by the Patriots, but New England lost on Sunday and is three games behind Buffalo in the loss column. Both 6-1 teams are in good shape even with a loss, and will look even stronger with a win. Because of the Vikings' competition within their division — and to a lesser extent, their quest to get the respect of being a legitimate Super Bowl contender — Minnesota needs it a little more.

The Vikings lost their last game at Detroit, with Jefferson having multiple passes thrown far off target to him, and he left the locker room without speaking to the media afterward. That was a clear sign he was upset. This week, Kyler Murray will sit out with a sore hamstring, leading to speculation he is being "soft benched." Even if that's not the case, having Carson Wentz at quarterback could help Jefferson, one of the league's best receivers who has been held back by bad quarterback play each of the last two seasons. The Bills are a good matchup for Jefferson. They've already allowed 1,078 yards and 11 touchdowns to receivers this season, via CBS. Getting Jefferson going again could revitalize a struggling Vikings offense.

The Vikings will be a home underdog for the first time this season when they take on Josh Allen and the 6-1 Bills. Some respected action has dropped the number from Bills -3.5 down to -3, but the betting public is overwhelmingly on Buffalo. Minnesota will give Carson Wentz the start in hopes that he can spark a bottom-five offense. Will he be able to get Justin Jefferson the ball and help run the offense? Minnesota's defense has been incredible so far, but even it has its limits. This should be a fun one. — Ben Fawkes

The winners of the 2026 Rawlings Gold Glove were announced Sunday night by Major League Baseball and, as expected, Cubs wunderkind Pete Crow-Armstrong took home his second straight National League Gold Glove in center field. PCA, who also won a Gold Glove in 2025 and is expected to be named the NL MVP in 2026, was the best defender in baseball this past season based on both the numbers and the eye test.

Here are the game's best defenders in 2026 according to Statcast's Fielding Runs Value, an all-encompassing metric that factors in range and arm, as well as blocking and framing for catchers:

Crow-Armstrong's +26 FRV is the fifth best in a single season since FRV launched in 2016 and the second best by a non-catcher, trailing only Nick Ahmed's +28 FRV season at shortstop in 2018.

Gold Gloves have be awarded since 1957 and are given to the best defensive player at each position in each league. That first year was one MLB-wide honor at each position. In 1958, Gold Gloves were split into AL and NL. Also, it used to be three outfielders per league regardless of exact position. Now the outfield spots are broken down into left field, center field, and right field.

Winners are determined through manager/coach voting (75%) and a statistical component (25%). Team employees can not vote for their own players.

While MLB announced "finalists" for each Gold Glove a few weeks back, remember that the voting was already complete and those finalists were simply the top three vote-getters at each position. This means, obviously, that postseason performance had no impact. Here now are the 2026 Gold Glove winners.

#2720. Kettering Town 'cannot hide' from its racism problem

Non-league Kettering Town have said they "can no longer hide" from the issue of racism after a visiting player was allegedly subjected to "sickening" abuse.

Redditch United player Dan Sweeney said he was targeted by a Kettering supporter during Saturday's Southern League Premier Division Central tie at the Poppies' Latimer Park stadium, which the hosts won 2-1.

The incident comes after a match official reported alleged racial abuse at a Kettering fixture last season, and a previous instance of alleged racist abuse against a Redditch player at Latimer Park in 2017.

In a statement, Kettering director of football Fabian Forde said the "poison" of racism went beyond matchdays.

He also spoke out against the presence of what he called "festering" racism on the club's fans forums.

Writing on the club's website, Forde said: "Let's be completely honest with ourselves: this is not the first time. We can no longer hide behind the comforting lie that 'it's just a small minority' or 'they don't reflect the majority of our fans'.

"Every single time we dismiss hate by calling it a minority issue, we minimise the damage. The truth is, if the majority stays silent, that small minority becomes our identity.

"They tarnish our reputation in the eyes of opposition players, fans, and officials. They make our club look like a haven for bigotry. Is that really who we want to be?"

Forde added that the club could not "keep sending out generic statements that mean nothing" and urged fans to support "real cultural change" by taking responsibility for calling out the perpetrators of racist abuse.

He said: "To the majority of our fans, the good, decent people who love this club for the right reasons, we are pleading with you.

"We need you to stand up. We need you to confront this minority head-on. If you see someone typing hate online, call them out. If you hear someone shouting abuse next to you on a Saturday afternoon, don't look away.

"Tell a steward. Identify them to the club. Why are we protecting people who are actively destroying the reputation of the club we love?"

Northamptonshire Police said Saturday's alleged incident had not yet been reported to officers [Getty Images]

Northamptonshire Police said they had "not identified any report relating to this [Saturday's] allegation."

However, the force added: "It may be that any report is awaiting allocation or has been made to another police force. Should a report be made elsewhere and the alleged offence be found to have taken place within Northamptonshire, we would take ownership of the investigation.

"We note Kettering Town FC's statement that it is working with its security team, stewards and the relevant authorities to identify those responsible, and we would encourage anyone who believes they have been the victim of a crime to report it to police.

"Racial abuse has no place in football or wider society, and any reports made to us will be assessed and investigated appropriately."

In a statement, Redditch United chairman David Faulkner said: "I particularly welcome Kettering Town's commitment to working with its security team, stewards and the relevant authorities to identify those responsible.

"It is vital that this matter is taken seriously and that appropriate action follows.

"Tackling racism requires more than statements. It requires leadership, accountability and a collective willingness to challenge unacceptable behaviour whenever and wherever it occurs.

"We must never allow incidents like this to become normalised, dismissed or simply forgotten once the immediate attention has passed."

The Football Association has also been approached for comment.

#2719. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

I'm done. No more. Enough is enough. I have doubted the Brewers far too many times and I decided in early August to never do it again. I started picking them to win the World Series every chance I got. I was finally right.

Every time they traded away someone good (the latest being Freddy Peralta last offseason), I thought, "OK, now is when it finally catches up with them." Only it never does. I thought they needed Tarik Skubal, both to reinforce their rotation and also to keep him away from the Dodgers. It didn't matter. They beat him and swept the Dodgers in the NLCS.

They develop young stars better than anyone. There's another one coming in Jesús Made, but there's no reason for Brewers fans to dream about the future when the present is World Series champions.

Jackson Chourio is becoming a superstar, Jacob Misiorowski is going to win the National League Cy Young and Christian Yelich is a former MVP, but it isn't really about the big names with this group. It's everything. It's the entire team making this train run, working as a cohesive unit. It's Robert Gasser going out and dealing in Game 3 after starting the season in the minors. It's Jake Bauers winning NLCS MVP not too long after he was ready to retire from baseball. It's Aaron Ashby putting up one of the greatest reliever performances in playoff history. It's Sal Frelick hitting a game-tying bomb. It's Cooper Pratt's coming-out party in the World Series. And on and on and on we could go.

Milwaukee is the best organization in baseball now, supplanting the former two-time defending champion Dodgers.

The Brewers head to next season with plenty of question marks, but they'll answer them. They always do. They are the champions of Major League Baseball and they sit atop the final 2026 Power Rankings.

Looking forward to next spring, my expectation is the Brewers will be No. 1. Some years, I write about why the defending champion is not No. 1. I've long since learned my lesson with this team, though. No more. The Brewers will be No. 1 heading into spring training.

#2715. 11 years ago, Avery Moses saved his family from a fire. Now, he's returning home to play basketball at UAlbany.

As a first grader, Avery Moses was hailed as a hero, with the city of Albany proclaiming a special day in his honor for his role in saving his family and their neighbors from a fire in their South End apartment building.

Almost exactly 11 years later, Moses – now a sought-after basketball recruit who moved to Texas while in middle school – announced that he's coming home to play his college basketball.

Now a 6-foot-4 guard who plays for Faith Family Academy of Oak Cliff in the Dallas area, Moses recently gave his verbal commitment to University at Albany men's basketball coach Dwayne Killings to join the Great Danes as a member of the recruiting class of 2027.

"I grew up in the 518," Moses said. "Coming back there and putting on for everyone who helped me along the way, that's really big."

It's been a long time since the events that led to then-Albany Mayor Kathy Sheehan proclaiming Moses as "our South End hero" for his actions during the Nov. 19, 2015 fire at his family's Broad Street apartment building.

Moses' keen sense of smell made him notice that something was off, and he quickly alerted his parents, Lynette and Anthony.

"I just remember smelling fire, smelling smoke," Moses said. "I was waking up my mom and dad, and we just got out of the house."

According to a Times Union report in the aftermath of the fire, Moses' persistence in waking up his family allowed the residents of the three-story building to escape unharmed.

On Nov. 30, 2015 - just a few days after Moses' seventh birthday - it was proclaimed as Avery Moses Day in the city of Albany during a ceremony at the Albany Fire Department's South End House.

For Moses, the memories of that day are a little foggy.

"I was really young, so I don't remember much," he said "I definitely do remember a lot of love from the city for doing what I did to get up out of there and help my family."

In the 11 years since, Moses has blossomed into a powerful guard who averaged 13.4 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.6 steals per game as a junior. Moses, who moved to Texas as an eighth grader, is rated as a three-star prospect by recruiting database 247 Sports, where he is ranked as the No. 244 prospect in the class of 2027.

He chose the Great Danes after drawing interest from a number of mid-major programs, including Northwestern State, Sam Houston State and the Air Force Academy.

"Coach Killings and his staff were really consistent (in their interest)," Moses said. "They showed a lot of love early on. That was the biggest thing, and that stuck with me."

On the court, Moses said his shooting and playmaking are currently the strongest aspects of his game.

"Whatever it takes to get my team to win," he said. "I hope to bring a lot of energy to Albany, and a lot of good vibes."

Moses is the third member of UAlbany's 2027 recruiting class, and the second with Capital Region ties. Troy native Treddy Faison, a former La Salle Institute star who now plays at Winchendon School in Massachusetts, was the first player to commit to the Great Danes this recruiting cycle. He was joined earlier this fall by Eli King, a standout guard at Eagle Academy in the Bronx.

This article originally published at 11 years ago, Avery Moses saved his family from a fire. Now, he's returning home to play basketball at UAlbany..

#2712. Tarik Skubal landing spots: Predicting new home for two-time Cy Young winner, the offseason's best free agent

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Arguably the best pitcher in baseball is up for grabs this winter. Tarik Skubal is a free agent for the 2026-27 MLB offseason, easily the top available on the market, and every team should be trying to earn his services. But will they? Almost certainly not.

The 29-year-old southpaw spent the first six years of his major-league career with the Detroit Tigers before being traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the 2026 deadline. He won back-to-back Cy Young awards in 2024 and 2025 and earned MVP votes in both seasons. He's likely to become the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history both in total value and AAV.

Of course, the giant flashing sign floating above all of this is the expiring CBA, which will run out at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, after which the owners are expected to lock out the players until a new deal is reached. Over the summer, the league proposed limiting free agency contracts, an offer that the players' union quickly disavowed, and the owners' demand for a salary cap is the underlying throughline of every negotiation. Perhaps that means Skubal will rush to sign on the dotted line before new rules are in place. Perhaps that means teams will wait out the negotiations until they know how much they have to spend -- and how they'll be punished if they do so.

Regardless, CBS Sports' MLB experts, three people who are very much not involved in contract negotiations, have gathered to predict where Skubal lands by the time Opening Day rolls around.

Mike Axisa: I'll go off the board a bit and say the Padres. The new ownership group didn't pay $3.9 billion for the franchise only to cheap out in their first offseason. They're moneyed and motivated, and that's usually enough to land the top free agents. It should appeal to Skubal too. The Padres are in the postseason most years, they play in a great (and largely pitcher-friendly) ballpark, and it's San Diego. How can you not love San Diego? Skubal to the Padres because the new owners want to make a big splash in their first offseason. That's my prediction.

Dayn Perry: I'll say the Mets top all offers by a margin sufficient to overcome their lack of appeal compared to the usual suspects (meaning, mostly, the Dodgers). They definitely need a stabilizing force in the rotation outside of Nolan McLean, and they also need a vibes shift after the deeply disappointing 2026 campaign. Landing the biggest fish of all on the market would provide all that and meet a clear need. The Mets will already be rebound candidates in 2027, and signing the likes of Skubal would position them as contenders. Obviously, the structure of the next CBA has bearing here, but maybe this all comes together before the lockout shuts it all down for an indeterminate period of time.

Matt Snyder: I'll go with the easy and obvious answer and say the Dodgers. I don't think the owners win the fight for a salary cap, but there'll be enough push from the Dodgers' end before the CBA talks shut down free agency to snatch up all the talent they can to get his contract grandfathered before a new agreement.

#2710. Kyle Whittingham says the starting quarterback for Michigan's game vs. No. 23 Oregon is TBD

Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham spoke to reporters at his weekly press conference on Monday.

Whittingham was asked about the firing of former offensive coordinator Jason Beck on Sunday, but he also looked ahead to this weekend's game against Oregon.

The Michigan head coach is apparently undecided on the starting quarterback, telling reporters it is "TBD" after the loss to Michigan State and the offensive coordinator change.

Michigan has used both Bryce Underwood and true freshman Tommy Carr as its starting quarterback this season. Whittingham even said Carr would be the team's starting quarterback for the "foreseeable future" after his performance against Rutgers on October 31.

After Michigan lost 15-6 against Michigan State last Saturday, though, the head coach has changed his tune. Whittingham said that Carr had a great game against Rutgers, but that the quarterback took a big drop-off against the Spartans. He added that Michigan needs better play from all its offensive units moving forward.

Underwood began the season as the incumbent starter but started slowly as the Wolverines infamously barely beat Western Michigan in a controversial Week 1 win, and then beat then-No. 11 Oklahoma 17-10.

The sophomore quarterback has seen action in seven of Michigan's games this year. Underwood has thrown for 924 yards, 5 touchdowns, and 6 interceptions, and has added 222 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.

Underwood was benched at halftime of Michigan's October 17 game against Penn State. Carr took over and led the Wolverines to a 21-18 win. After that, he started against Indiana, but Michigan lost 13-6 in overtime.

Carr and the Wolverines bounced back with a 28-21 win over Rutgers, but then lost to Michigan State last weekend.

The true freshman has played in five games and has thrown for 641 yards, 2 touchdowns, and 3 interceptions. Carr has added 95 yards and three touchdowns on the ground.

After the loss to Michigan State, Michigan is now 5-4 but is 2-4 in Big Ten play this year.

The Wolverines will take the road to face No. 23 Oregon this weekend, then end the season with games against undefeated No. 8 UCLA, followed by "The Game" on the road against No. 12 Ohio State.

#2709. MLB rumors: Early favorites for Tarik Skubal emerge, plus Astros eye old friend in hunt for new manager

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is upon us. The Milwaukee Brewers won the belt and the title, and they're now in the process of being feted far and wide. Meantime, an uncertain hot stove season is preparing to unfold. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 1 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22.

Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are already flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Monday's supply just below.

Ace and, for now, back-to-back American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal is far and away the most coveted free agent within the current class, and he's almost certain to ink a contract well past the $300 million mark and perhaps the largest contract ever for a pitcher.

On that front, the incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers, who acquired Skubal from the Detroit Tigers in a deadline trade; the New York Mets; and the Chicago Cubs are expected to be the leading contenders for the lefty's services, ESPN reports. The Cubs, though, may not be willing to go as high as the Dodgers and Mets may be, and of those two, the Mets at this juncture are expected to be the more vigorous in their pursuit of Skubal.
